title: The minimum you need to know about GitHub Actions
why_read: A beginner-level introduction to GitHub Actions aimed at readers who have never used CI/CD, offering little new information for experienced engineers.
analysis: This is an entry-level tutorial explaining GitHub Actions as an automation tool, illustrated with the author's personal use case of auto-building and deploying a Hugo static site. It covers only the very basics, workflow file structure and a six-line example, without going into advanced patterns like matrix builds, caching, reusable workflows, or security considerations. It's a fine onboarding resource for complete beginners but has essentially no new technical content for anyone who already uses CI/CD.
